correctness.rationale: For n>=3 the connected double covers are exactly nontrivial sign classes. Len–Zakharov's published Theorem 3.4 gives the normalized squared Prym volume as a sum of odd genus-one decompositions. For a two-vertex n-edge banana every such decomposition consists of n−2 edges; its complement is a two-edge cycle with nontrivial monodromy iff the two signs differ, and its rank equals one, giving Q(s)=Σ_{i<j}w_ij(1−s_i s_j)/2. Singleton/two-edge cut inclusion-exclusion yields each w_ij. Multiplying all w_ij yields P=product_i length_i and a positive-root formula recovers each edge. Fourier inversion on the even-character basis gives the exact image conditions: higher bands vanish, pair coefficients are negative, and positive w obey all four-index tetrads. The positive tetrads are sufficient for a unique multiplicative rank-one factorization w_ij=u_i u_j (including n=3); rescaling u produces positive lengths; Q(1)=0 fixes its Fourier constant. No limiting/experimental inference is used. Included exact Fraction verification reconstructs nonuniform cases n=3..7 and a nonrealizable positive profile.

originality.rationale: The scientific target is simultaneous inverse recognition of all labeled free-double-cover squared Prym volumes on banana strata. The closest directly relevant general literature gives a forward Kirchhoff–Prym volume polynomial, not a theorem recovering lengths and characterizing the semialgebraic image of the entire volume-profile map. The nearest compared published tropical banana claim concerns a mu-polystable complex, not labeled Prym volumes. Other inspected research results concern different invariants. value.rationale: A numerical Prym volume usually loses period data, and asking whether the family of all double-cover scalar volumes can recover the original metric is a natural Torelli-type inverse problem. The theorem provides a sharp positive result for every genus>=2 banana stratum, a constructive inverse using only singleton/pair-cover data, and an exact Fourier/tetrad semialgebraic membership test for arbitrary proposed volume profiles. The n=3 strict triangle inequalities and n=4 codimension-three constraints make falsifiable image restrictions; a positive weighted cut profile can still fail to come from any positive metric banana. This goes beyond tabulating a finite invariant or merely rewriting the established forward volume formula.
